args.message:
fix(payments): use ROUND_HALF_EVEN for money rounding (FIN-212)

src/money.py claimed to implement banker's rounding but quantized with
ROUND_HALF_UP, so half-cent values rounded away from even. Switch to
ROUND_HALF_EVEN to match the documented FIN-212 behaviour and the
expectations in tests/test_money.py.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: fix(payments): use ROUND_HALF_EVEN for money rounding (FIN-212)
args.body:
## Problem

The nightly build of `payments-service` fails: `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was quantizing with `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

Half-cent amounts therefore rounded away from even, e.g. `Decimal("2.665")` rounded to `2.67` instead of the expected `2.66`.

## Change

- `src/money.py`: switch `round_money()` from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (single-line behaviour change, import updated). No API change — signature and return type are unchanged.

## Verification

- CI run `ci-0001` on this branch: **passed** (tests green, including the FIN-212 half-even cases).

## Notes

This is a bug fix only; no other call sites rely on half-up rounding. Requesting review from @alex. Merge into protected `main` requires code-owner approval.
